title: Gaze into the Pattern: Characterizing Spatial Patterns with Internal Temporal Correlations for Hardware Prefetching
problem: Existing spatial-region hardware prefetchers predict memory access footprints using system-level context features (trigger PC, data address) that fail to capture the intrinsic characteristics of spatial access patterns, resulting in poor flexibility and suboptimal prefetch accuracy across diverse workloads.
motivation: As memory latency gaps widen, effective hardware prefetching becomes critical; conventional spatial region prefetchers over-rely on external context rather than the internal structure of spatial footprints, limiting adaptability.
method: Gaze extracts footprint-internal temporal correlations — the ordering and timing relationships among cache line accesses within a spatial region — as the primary feature for characterizing and predicting spatial access patterns. This avoids dependence on trigger PC or address-based context lookup. For spatial streaming patterns (very high access density within a region), Gaze applies a dedicated two-stage prefetch approach to suppress over-prefetching: a first stage filters high-density streaming footprints and a second stage applies targeted prefetch decisions to avoid redundant prefetches.
key_novelty: Using footprint-internal temporal correlation (access ordering within spatial regions) rather than external context (trigger PC/address) as the core feature for spatial pattern characterization in a hardware prefetcher.
contributions: Identification that internal temporal correlations within spatial footprints are a more effective characterization feature than system-level context for spatial prefetching.
Gaze hardware spatial prefetcher using footprint-internal temporal correlations for pattern matching and prediction.
Two-stage approach mitigating over-prefetching in high-density spatial streaming scenarios.
5.7%/5.4% single-core and 11.4%/8.8% eight-core performance improvement vs. PMP and vBerti (recent low-cost baselines).

metrics.speedup: 5.7% and 5.4% single-core; 11.4% and 8.8% eight-core IPC improvement vs. PMP and vBerti respectively

limitations: The temporal correlation approach assumes stable intra-footprint access ordering; highly irregular or pointer-chasing workloads with non-recurring spatial patterns may not benefit.
primary_theme: Spatial hardware prefetching using intra-footprint temporal correlations
